title: Faithfully flat local comparison through a common field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $E/k$, $L/k$ arbitrary field extensions [def-pc-field-extension]. Let $R$ be a commutative $k$-algebra, $R_E=R\otimes_kE$, $S=R\otimes_kL$, $\mathfrak q$ a prime ideal of $S$, and $\mathfrak p$ its inverse image under $R\to S$. Tensor products use [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] with their usual algebra multiplication. There exist a field $F$, embeddings $i_E:E\to F$ and $i_L:L\to F$ agreeing on $k$, and a prime ideal $\mathfrak Q$ of $T=R\otimes_kF$ whose inverse image under $S\to T$, $r\otimes l\mapsto r\otimes i_L(l)$, is $\mathfrak q$. Let $\mathfrak P$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak Q$ under $R_E\to T$, $r\otimes e\mapsto r\otimes i_E(e)$. Then $\mathfrak P$ contracts to $\mathfrak p$ in $R$, and the induced map
$$(R_E)_{\mathfrak P}\longrightarrow T_{\mathfrak Q},\qquad t/u\longmapsto i(t)/i(u),$$
is a faithfully flat local homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], where $i:R_E\to T$ is the displayed scalar-extension map and local means that the inverse image of the maximal ideal is the maximal ideal. Both $S\to T$ and $R_E\to T$ are faithfully flat. No algebraicity, finite degree, Noetherianity, or finite generation is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0384 (lemma-geometrically-reduced-upstairs), reverse implication: common extension, point above the prescribed point, and the faithfully flat map of local rings; field amalgamation is fields.tex Tag 0H7K (lemma-common-extension-field).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-common-extension-fields] to the given extensions $E/k$ and $L/k$. Obtain a field $F$ and $k$-embeddings $i_E:E\to F$ and $i_L:L\to F$. Give $F$ its $E$- and $L$-algebra structures through these embeddings; their restrictions to $k$ agree. Put $T=R\otimes_kF$.

For each $H\in\{E,L\}$ write $i_H:H\to F$ for its chosen embedding and $R_H=R\otimes_kH$. The tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives mutually inverse ring maps
$$\alpha_H:(R\otimes_kH)\otimes_HF\longrightarrow T,\quad (r\otimes h)\otimes f\longmapsto r\otimes i_H(h)f,\qquad \beta_H:T\longrightarrow(R\otimes_kH)\otimes_HF,\quad r\otimes f\longmapsto(r\otimes1)\otimes f.$$
The formulas respect balancing: replacing $rh_0\otimes h$ by $r\otimes h_0h$ for $h_0\in k$ has the same image because $i_H$ is a $k$-map, and $((r\otimes h)a)\otimes f=(r\otimes h)\otimes i_H(a)f$ for $a\in H$. Both formulas preserve products and $1$. On a pure tensor, $\alpha_H\beta_H(r\otimes f)=r\otimes f$ and $\beta_H\alpha_H((r\otimes h)\otimes f)=(r\otimes1)\otimes i_H(h)f=(r\otimes h)\otimes f$. The generation clause of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] extends these equalities to every element. Thus $\alpha_H$ is an isomorphism, and it sends $x\otimes1$ to the stated scalar-extension map $j_H(x)$; this follows on $x=r\otimes h$ and then by additivity.

source.place: Tag 0384, common-extension base change, explicit tensor identification

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] with base field $H$, extension $F/H$, and commutative $H$-algebra $R_H$, for $H=E$ and $H=L$. It gives faithful flatness of $R_H\to R_H\otimes_HF$. Under $\alpha_H$ from Step 2 this is $j_H:R_H\to T$. Indeed $\alpha_H$ is $R_H$-linear for these actions, so tensoring any complex over $R_H$ with either target gives isomorphic complexes; the exactness criterion in [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] is therefore unchanged. Consequently both $R_E\to T$ and $S=R_L\to T$ are faithfully flat, and in particular flat.

source.place: Tag 0384, field-extension maps are flat; faithful flatness before localization

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] to $j_L:S\to T$ and the prescribed prime $\mathfrak q$. It supplies a prime $\mathfrak Q\subset T$ with $j_L^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)=\mathfrak q$. Define $\mathfrak P=j_E^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)$. It is prime: $1$ is not in it, and $ab\in\mathfrak P$ implies $j_E(a)j_E(b)\in\mathfrak Q$, hence $a\in\mathfrak P$ or $b\in\mathfrak P$. For $r\in R$, both composites $R\to R_E\to T$ and $R\to S\to T$ send $r$ to $r\otimes1$. Therefore $r\otimes1\in\mathfrak P$ if and only if $r\otimes1\in\mathfrak Q$ if and only if $r\otimes1\in\mathfrak q$, which is exactly $r\in\mathfrak p$. This proves the required contraction to $R$.

source.place: Tag 00HQ (lemma-ff-rings); point lifting in varieties.tex Tag 0384

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] for the flat ring map $j_E:R_E\to T$ and the prime $\mathfrak Q$, whose inverse image is $\mathfrak P$ by Step 4. Its conclusion gives a flat local homomorphism $f:(R_E)_{\mathfrak P}\to T_{\mathfrak Q}$, with exactly the formula $t/u\mapsto j_E(t)/j_E(u)$. No Noetherian clause of that node is used. To check the stronger inverse-image description of locality explicitly, a fraction $t/u$ belongs to the maximal ideal of $(R_E)_{\mathfrak P}$ precisely when $t\in\mathfrak P$, and its image belongs to the maximal ideal of $T_{\mathfrak Q}$ precisely when $j_E(t)\in\mathfrak Q$; these are equivalent by definition of $\mathfrak P$. Denominators are valid because $u\notin\mathfrak P$ implies $j_E(u)\notin\mathfrak Q$. Here the maximal ideals are the extended primes as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization); the flat local map in varieties.tex Tag 0384

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] to the two local rings and the flat local homomorphism $f$ from Step 5. This proves its faithful flatness. Together with the field embeddings of Step 1, the two faithful flatness conclusions of Step 3, and the prime and contraction identities of Step 4, this gives every assertion. The construction uses arbitrary field extensions and arbitrary commutative algebras throughout.
